answers.answer: Plot the points (0, -1), (1, 1) and (2, 3) on a coordinate plane.
solution: Draw the horizontal x-axis and the vertical y-axis, meeting at O.
Mark the integers on both axes.
Plot (0, -1): at 0 on the x-axis, then 1 unit down, on the y-axis.
Each ordered pair is one and only one point.

answers.answer: X×Y = Y×X when X = Y (the two sets are the same).
solution: The lesson says X×Y ≠ Y×X when X ≠ Y.
So the two products can be equal only when X and Y are the same set.
If X = Y then X×Y = X×X = Y×X.

solution: Plot (3, 5): go 3 along the x-axis, then 5 up.
Plot (5, 3): go 5 along the x-axis, then 3 up.

Each ordered pair is represented by one and only one point, so different points mean different pairs.

Equal ordered pairs have equal first projections and equal second projections.

answers.answer: Arrow diagram of X × Y = {(1,3),(1,4),(1,5),(2,3),(2,4),(2,5)}: six arrows from X to Y.
solution: Draw an oval for X on the left containing 1 and 2.
Draw an oval for Y on the right containing 3, 4 and 5.
Draw an arrow from each element of X (first projection) to each element of Y (second projection).
From 1 draw arrows to 3, to 4 and to 5.
From 2 draw arrows to 3, to 4 and to 5.
This gives 6 arrows, one for each ordered pair.

answers.answer: Cartesian diagram: a grid with X = 1, 2 on the horizontal line and Y = 3, 4, 5 on the vertical line, with the 6 intersection points marked as the pairs of X × Y.
solution: Draw a horizontal line and mark 1 and 2 on it, for the elements of X.
Draw a vertical line and mark 3, 4 and 5 on it, for the elements of Y.
Mark the 6 points where these lines cross.

answers.answer: Use a perpendicular graphical net, with the set marked on both the horizontal and vertical lines, where each intersection point is one ordered pair.
solution: Draw two perpendicular lines x'x (horizontal) and y'y (vertical) meeting at O, which represents 0.
For N × N, mark the natural numbers on both lines starting from O.
For Z × Z, mark the integers on both lines, with O as (0, 0). The net is the coordinate plane of Z × Z.
For Q × Q, mark the rational numbers on both lines in the same way.
For R × R, mark the real numbers on both lines. The net is divided into four quadrants.
Draw vertical and horizontal lines through the marked points. Each intersection point represents one ordered pair of the product.
Read from the Z × Z net: A is 2 units right of O on the x-axis and 3 units up.
Read from the Z × Z net: B is 3 units right of O and 2 units down.
Read from the Z × Z net: C is 3 units left of O and 1 unit up.
Read from the Z × Z net: D is 3 units left of O and 4 units down.

answers.answer: A(3, 5/2): plot the point 3 units right of O and 5/2 units up.
solution: Draw perpendicular lines x'x and y'y meeting at O.
Mark the rational numbers on both lines, including halves such as 5/2 = 2.5.
From 3 on the x-axis draw a vertical line.
From 5/2 on the y-axis draw a horizontal line.

answers.answer: B(-3/2, 4): plot the point 3/2 units left of O and 4 units up.
solution: Use the same net with the rational numbers marked on both lines.
From -3/2 = -1.5 on the x-axis draw a vertical line.
From 4 on the y-axis draw a horizontal line.

answers.answer: C(-3, -3/2): plot the point 3 units left of O and 3/2 units down.
solution: Use the same net with the rational numbers marked on both lines.
From -3 on the x-axis draw a vertical line.
From -3/2 = -1.5 on the y-axis draw a horizontal line.

answers.answer: D(5/2, -3/2): plot the point 5/2 units right of O and 3/2 units down.
solution: Use the same net with the rational numbers marked on both lines.
From 5/2 = 2.5 on the x-axis draw a vertical line.
From -3/2 = -1.5 on the y-axis draw a horizontal line.
